title: spec review: S1f env_policy: allowlisted environment propagation for worker subprocesses (off/shadow/active), names-only shadow log, never a secret value (P22)
spec:
Create orchestrator/env_policy.py. worker_env(role, *, base, extra, cfg) -> (env, stripped): base is the parent environment mapping, extra the keys the caller must set (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ORCH_TASK_ID, oauth token env for the account, resolved [secrets.<role>] keys), cfg the pool config. Config in .orchestrator/pool.toml [secrets]: env_mode = "shadow" (values off, shadow, active; add with a dated comment) and env_passthrough = ["PATH","HOME","USER","LOGNAME","LANG","LC_ALL","TERM","SHELL","TMPDIR","XDG_*","CLAUDE_*","ORCH_*","UV_*","VIRTUAL_ENV","PYTHONPATH","NODE_*","GIT_*","SSH_AUTH_SOCK"] (glob patterns; defaults used when absent). Rules: active -> env contains only base keys matching the passthrough patterns plus every extra key; shadow -> env is base plus extra unchanged, but stripped lists the keys active would have removed; off -> no computation, stripped empty. Keys whose name contains KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL or AUTH are never passed through by pattern in active mode unless named exactly in extra or listed in [secrets.<role>] (so CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN reaches the worker only because spawn passes it as extra). Shadow and active both log one runs row via bus.log_run(role="env_policy", task=..., outcome=mode, stripped=<sorted key names>, count=n) — key names only, never values; the row must never raise.
Wire: spawn.py where the claude -p env is built (around line 1020-1025) and executor.py where codex exec subprocesses get their environment (find the subprocess call; if it inherits os.environ implicitly, pass env explicitly). Also audit and document (docs/hermes-hardening/06-credential-filtering.md): which env keys the current machine would strip in active mode (names only, measured by running worker_env against os.environ in shadow and listing the names), where jev.redact already applies, and that logs never carry values. Do not change [secrets.<role>] resolution. Test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped.
Spec review T-1089 folded in: (1) The credential-name veto matches whole underscore-separated name tokens (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL, CREDENTIALS, AUTH), so GIT_AUTHOR_NAME (token AUTHOR) passes; an env_passthrough entry that is an exact name (no wildcard) overrides the veto, which is how the default SSH_AUTH_SOCK survives; glob entries never override it. (2) worker_env(role, *, base, extra, cfg, task_id=None): the runs row uses task_id; spawn passes the task id, executor passes task_id, goals/planner_shadow pass the goal or launch id. (3) Scope adds orchestrator/goals.py (_create_goal_task and launch_planner claude -p environments) and orchestrator/planner_shadow.py (launch): every claude -p or codex exec environment the orchestrator builds goes through worker_env, so the audit doc covers all spawn paths (list them). (4) executor.py: role execute, extra = ORCH_TASK_ID plus the resolved [secrets.execute] keys when that table exists, plus CODEX_HOME and HOME when set (codex reads its auth from there); shadow first, and the doc lists (names only) what active mode would strip from the codex environment on this machine so the human decides the flip.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Read docs/context-economy/00-overview.md only if you need the evidence/decision_log conventions.
acceptance: tests/test_env_policy.py::test_active_mode_allowlists_and_keeps_extra (a base env with secret-looking names is stripped, PATH and ORCH_* kept, extra keys kept)
tests/test_env_policy.py::test_shadow_mode_only_reports (env unchanged, stripped names listed, log row written with names only)
tests/test_env_policy.py::test_log_row_never_contains_values (a synthetic value never appears in the runs row)
tests/test_spawn.py::test_spawn_uses_env_policy (patched Popen receives the env from worker_env; oauth token passed as extra)
tests/test_env_policy.py::test_token_veto_and_exact_name_override (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME passes, SSH_AUTH_SOCK passes via exact entry, a name with the token TOKEN is stripped)
tests/test_env_policy.py::test_all_spawn_paths_use_worker_env (spawn, executor, goals, planner_shadow patched launches receive worker_env output)

risks.issue: _create_goal_task (line 115) sets ORCH_ROOT and ORCH_GOAL_TEXT as ad-hoc overrides on os.environ, and launch_planner (line 334) and planner_shadow.launch (planner_shadow.py:50) likewise override ORCH_ROOT (and ORCH_SHADOW). None of these three keys are in the spec's fixed extra list (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ORCH_TASK_ID, oauth token env, resolved [secrets.<role>] keys). ORCH_* matches the default env_passthrough glob, so in active mode worker_env would pass through whatever ORCH_ROOT/ORCH_GOAL_TEXT happen to already be in the base os.environ of the orchestrator process (usually absent or stale) instead of the per-call computed value, since passthrough only preserves existing base keys, not caller overrides. goals.py:35 does 'os.environ["ORCH_GOAL_TEXT"]' with no .get default, so a goal-creation subprocess spawned under active mode raises KeyError immediately, and any worktree-scoped worker gets the wrong ORCH_ROOT. This is dormant in shadow mode (env is unchanged) and only breaks when env_mode flips to active, so the acceptance suite as scoped (generic 'receives worker_env output' checks) would not catch it.
launch() also sets ORCH_SHADOW="1" outside the spec's extra list, same class of bug as ORCH_ROOT/ORCH_GOAL_TEXT above — silently dropped or stale in active mode.

[secrets.scout] etc. are already declared (line 364) without a preceding bare [secrets] header; TOML requires a table's own key=value pairs to be written before any of its dotted subtables are declared, so env_mode/env_passthrough must be inserted as a new [secrets] header placed above the existing [secrets.scout] block, not appended after it. Worth stating explicitly so the diff doesn't land after the subtables and fail to parse.

suggested_spec_changes: Enumerate the call-specific env keys per site instead of one fixed extra list: goals.py _create_goal_task needs ORCH_ROOT + ORCH_GOAL_TEXT in extra; goals.py launch_planner and planner_shadow.py launch need ORCH_ROOT (planner_shadow.py also ORCH_SHADOW) in extra, in addition to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/oauth token/resolved secrets.

Add an acceptance test that asserts ORCH_ROOT (and ORCH_GOAL_TEXT / ORCH_SHADOW at their respective call sites) survive worker_env in active mode even when absent from base os.environ, not just that Popen received worker_env's output.

Note in the pool.toml scope item that the new [secrets] env_mode/env_passthrough keys must be inserted before the existing [secrets.scout] subtable line, since TOML forbids a table's own keys after its subtables are declared.
